IS : 1017 - 1983 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR CHAMOIS LEATHER 

( Second Revision ) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 30 June 1983, after the draft finalized by the 
Leather Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical 
Division Council. 

0.2 This standard was first published in 1957 and then revised in 1966, 
incorporating Amendment No. 1 and enlarging the scope of this 
standard to include chamois leather used as linings in orthopaedic 
appliances. Consequent upon the supersession of IS : 1016-1956* and at 
the specific request of the Ministry of Defence, the second revision 
was undertaken to update the methods of test reference to Indian Standards 
and recasting the text. , 

0.3 Chamois leather is produced in India mostly from goatskin though in 
foreign countries it is made from sheepskin and to a limited extent from 
calf and deer skins also. Chamois leather is available in different grades 
depending on the end use. Grade I of chamois leather is usfed by the 
defence services and in engineering industries for filtering ' petrol to 
remove moisture, while the other grades are mainly used for polishing and 
cleaning purposes. Chamois leather is also used in the manufacture of 
ladies hand gloves, apparel use, lining of binocular cases and in packing 
ammunition. As lining leather, chamois leather finds application in the 
manufacture of orthopaedic appliances. 

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off m 
accordance with IS : 2-1960J. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value 
in this standard. 



• Methods of sampling and test for oil tanned leathers. 
fRulea for rounding off numerical values ( revised). 



IS : 1017 - 1983 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements, the method of sampling 
and test for chamois leather used for filtering petrol, cleaning optical 
instruments and polished surfaces, glove manufacture, orthopaedic 
purposes, apparel use, and lining or padding of leather goods. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS: 1640- 
1960* shall apply. 

3. GRADES 

3.1 This standard specifies three grades of materials as follows: 

Grade 1 Heavy quality suitable for petrol Alteration and glove 
manufacture. 

Grade 2 Heavy quality suitable for polishing surfaces. 

Grade 3 Light quality suitable for general use, orthopaedic purpose 
and apparel use, etc. 

4. DESCRIPTION 

4.1 Grade 1 — The material shall be free from physical defects, namely, 
holes, scratches, cuts and hard, thin or uneven patches. It shall be free 
from any stitching. 

4.2 Grade 2 — The material shall be reasonably free from physical 
defects, namely, holes, scratches and cuts. Cuts and holes shall be properly 
sewn and shall not affect the serviceability of the skin. The number of 
stitchings shall be not more than 10/m 2 . It shall also be suitable for 
cleaning polished surfaces without leaving any scratch on the surface. 

4.3 Grade 3 — The material shall be the same as Grade 2, but shall 
be lighter in substance ( see Table 2 ). 

5. REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 Raw Material — The material shall be goatskins or sheepskins. 

5.2 Tanning — The material shall be manufactured by straight oil 
tannage by using cod or other fish oil or combination tannage, by using 
formaldehyde and cod or other fish oil. 



•Glossary of terms relating to hides, skins and leather. 

4 



IS : 1017 - 1983 

5.3 Finishing — The material, after stuffing with oil followed by 
oxidation, shall be degrassed. It shall be wrung out, dried and buffed on 
boths side to produce a velvety nap. It shall be free from dust particles 
as far as possible. 

Note — No degreasing shall be done by solvent. 
5.3.1 The material shall not be chemically bleached or dyed. 

5.4 Size — Unless otherwise required, chamois leather shall be supplied 
either in rectangular or natural shape, as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the supplier. If supplied in natural shape, the edges shall be well 
trimmed and the area of the skins measured either by a measuring 
machine or by planimeter. 

5.5 Chemical Requirements — The material shall comply with the 
chemical requirements given in Table 1 when tested by the methods 
prescribed in IS : 582-1970*. Reference to the relevant clauses of IS : 582- 
1970* is given in col 6 of the table.

5.7 Specific Requirements for Orthopaedic Purposes — In 

addition to the requirements prescribed under 5*5 and 5.6, except for 
water soluble matter and ash content which shall not exceed 3'0 percent, 
in both the cases, for all grades, the material for orthopaedic purposes 
shall comply with the following requirements. 



IS : 1017 - 1983 

5/7.1 Free Formaldehyde — Free formaldehyde in the material shall not 
exceed 0*1 percent by mass, when tested in accordance with LC: 14 of 
IS : 582-1970*. 

5.7.2 p// of Water Extract — The p\l of the water extract shall be 
between 4*5 and iVO, when tested in accordance with LC: 18 of IS : 582- 
1970*. 

5.7.3 Water Soluble Chlorides — An aqueous extract of the material 
shall contain not more than 0.5 percent by mass of sodium chloride when 
tested in accordance with LC: 19 of IS : 582-1970*. 

5.7.4 Water Soluble Sulphates — An aqueous extract of the material shall 
contain not more than 025 percent by mass of sodium sulphate when 
tested in accordance with LC: 20 of IS : 582-1970*. 

5.8 Optional Requirements for Defence Purposes — In addition 
to the requirements given under 5.5 and 5.6, chamois leather for certain 
defence purposes shall comply with the requirements given in 5.7.2, 5.7.3 
and 5.7.4. The indentor shall clearly indicate this requirement while 
indenting the material. 

6. MARKING AND PACKING 

6.1 On each piece of the leather, its area in dm : shall be legibly marked. 

6.2 The leather shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and 
the supplier. 

6.3 The package shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer; 
grade; recognized trade-mark, if any; number of pieces of leather; and 
month and year of manufacture. 

6.3.1 The packages and 'or skins may also be marked with the ISI 
Certification Mark. 

Notk — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of 
the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks )Act and the Rules and Regu- 
lations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have boon produced to comply with the requirements 
of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI 
marked products arc also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, 
may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 



♦Methods for chemical testing of leather {first revision ). 

7 



IS i 1017 - 1983 

7. SAMPLING 

7.1 The scale of sampling, position of sampling of test pieces shall be as 
prescribed in IS : 5868-1983*. Conditioning of test pieces shall be as 
prescribed in LP : of IS : 5914-19701. Criteria for conformity shall be 
as prescribed in 7.2 to 7.4. 

7.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the chemical requirements 
as stipulated in this standard, the test result of the prepared sample shall 
lie within the specified value in each case, as given in Table 1. 

7.3 In case of physical requirements like sink test; and mass of chamois 
leather, the value Xzb2s shall lie within the limits prescribed in Table 2. 
In the case of water absorption test and petrol Alteration test X— 2s shall 
be equal to or greater than the minimum specified in Table 2, All the 
samples drawn and tested for surface defects and wet exposure test shall 
satisfy the respective requirements. A' is the mean and s is the standard 
deviation. For calculating these factors, see Appendix G. 

7.4 If for any one of the characteristics, the requirement of 7.2 and 7.3 

are not satisfied the lot shall be rejected. 



APPENDIX A 

[ Clause 5.6, Table 2, SI No, (i) ] 

DETERMINATION OF MASS PER UNIT AREA 

A-l. TEST SPECIMEN 

A-l.l All the pieces of leather sample shall be tested. 

A-2. CONDITIONING 

A-2.1 All the pieces of leather sample shall be conditioned as prescribed 
in LP: Oof IS : 5914-1970t 

A-3. PROCEDURE 

A«3»l Take all pieces of leather to be sampled as prescribed in 7*1. 
Weigh them and measure their area preferably by a leather measuring 
machine if available, otherwise by hand. If, however, the leather pieces 
be of rectangular shape, measure the area by means of a tape, without 
having recourse to a measuring machine, as in A-3.2, 



'Methods of sampling for leattot (Jmsi rtoisitn). 
fMethods of physical testing of leather.

IS : 1017 - 1983 

A-3.2 Measure the length LL' and the breadth WW ( set Fig. 1 ) by 
means of a tape. 




Fig. 1 Measurement of Area 

A-4. CALCULATION 

A-4.1 Calculate the arithmetic mean of the mass per square metre of all 
the test specimens and their standard deviation s as given in Appendix G. 
Report the average mass per square metre of the leather as Ji±2j where 
X is the mean value. 

APPENDIX B 

[ Clause 5.6, Table 2, SI No. (ii) ] 
DETERMINATION OF WATER ABSROPTION 

B-l. TEST SPECIMEN 

B-l.l One test per sample piece selected as prescribed in 7.1 shall be 
taken for the determination of water absorption. Samples for test shall be 



IS 1 161? - 1983 

representative of the butts, bellies and shoulders in equal proportion to 
the leather pieces selected. Cut a disc from the sample piece with a 
circular diameter of 3 cm. 

B-2. CONDITIONING OF TEST SPECIMEN 

B-2.1 Prior to evaluation, test specimen shall be conditioned as prescribed 
in LP: Oof IS: 5914-1970*. 

B-3. PROCEDURE 

B-3.1 Weigh the conditioned test specimen; soak in 25 ml of distilled water 
at 21°C in a tared covered dish for 30 minutes. Remove the test specimen 
with forceps, draining the adhering water back into the dish for 
2 minutes. Do not blot the piece. Weigh the sample and evaporate the 
aqueous solution to dryness and weigh the residue. 

B-4. CALCULATION

B-4.1 Calculate the arithmetic mean of the water absorption of all the 
test specimens and their standard deviation s as given in Appendix A. 
Report the average water absorption of the bulk of leather as Xj^2s 
where X is the mean value. 



appendix c 

[ Clause 5.6, Table 2, SI No. (iii) ] 
SINKING TEST 

C-l. TEST SPECIMEN 

G-l.l One test per sample piece selected in accordance witih 7.1 shall 
be taken for the determination of sinking test. Samples for test shall be 



•Method* of pfaycical tetting of leather. 

10 



IS : 1017 * 1983 

representative of the butts, bellies and shoulders in equal proportion 
of the leather pieces selected. Cut a piece of 1 1 x 1 cm size from the 
sample piece with a sharp knife. 

C-2. CONDITIONING OF TEST SPECIMEN 

C-2.1 Prior to evaluation test specimen shall be conditioned as prescribed 
in LP: Oof IS : 5914-1970*. 

C-3. PROCEDURE 

C-3.1 Fill water to a height of 19 cm in a two-litre beaker. Place the 
test specimen on the surface of water carefully and then note the time 
taken for the test specimen to sink completely to the bottom of the 
beaker. 

Note — If there be present any uncombined oil inside the leather, the leather 
will be lighter in mass and consequently will take longer time to sink. 

C-4. CALCULATION 

C-4.1 Calculate arithmetic mean of the time taken by all the test 
specimens to sink and their standard deviation s as given in Appendix A. 
Report average sinking time of the bulk leather as X±2s where -? is the 
mean value. 



APPENDIX D 

[ Clause 5.6, Table 2, SI No. (iv) ] 
TEST FOR WET EXPOSURE 
D-l. TEST SPECIMEN 

D-Ll One test per sample piece selected is accordance with 7#1 shall be 
taken for the determination of wet exposure test. The samples per test 
shall be representative of the butts, bellies and shoulders in equal 
proportion of the leather pieces selected. Gut a test piece approximately 
7*5 cm square. 

D-2. PROCEDURE 

D-2.1 Introduce the test piece in a 250-ml flask containing 100 ml of 
distilled water. Place the flask in a thermostatically controlled oven at a 



•Methods of physical testing of leather. 

11 



IS: 1017-1983 

temperature of 45±1°C. Maintain the flask containing the specimen at 
this temperature for seven days. Take out the specimen after seven days 
and examine for sliminess. Dry the test piece at room temperature. Pull 
out the dry piece and compare its feel and appearance with an original 
piece cut to the same dimensions as the test specimen. 



APPENDIX E 

[ Clause 5.6, Table 2, SI No. (v) ] 

TEST FOR PETROL FILTRATION 

El. TEST SPECIMEN 

E-l.l All pieces of leather sample shall be tested. 

E-2. PROCEDURE 

E-2.1 Prepare a mixture of petrol and water using 430 ml of gasoline 
( 70 octane ) and 30 ml of water. 

E-2.2 Take a full size skin, and wet it in dry gasoline ( 70 octane ). 
Squeeze the skin and insert it on a glass funnel 18 cm in diameter. Pour 
the petrol-water mixture through the skin and record with the help of a 
stop watch the time required for the first drop of water to pass through 
the skin after all the petrol has passed through. The time shall be 
reckoned from the commencement of the test. 

E-3. CALCULATION 

E-3.1 Calculate the arithmetic mean of the time taken for the first drop 
of water to pass through, and their standard deviation s as given in 
Appendix G. 

APPENDIX F 

[ Clause 5.6, Table 2, SI No. (vi) ] 

CARE AND MAINTENANCE OF CHAMOIS LEATHER FOR 
PETROL FILTRATION 

F-l. PERIODIC TESTING 

F-l.l Examine the chamois leathers for holes, drift and moisture 
immediately before and after they are used for petrol filtration. If 

12 



IS : 1017 - 1983 

chamois leather is used regularly (everyday) subject it to petrol 
filtration test ( see Table 2 ) once every 14 days and once every 2 months 
if the chamois leather is used occasionally. Maintain records of all such 
tests and their results for individual chamois leather. 

F-2. STORAGE 

F-2.1 Roll round a rod and store spare chamois leathers in cylindrical 
containers which should be free from dampness. Do not fold, store, damp 
or wet chamois leather. 

F-3. INSPECTION 

F-3«l After a chamois leather has been used for filtering petrol to remove 
dirt and moisture, examine carefully for signs of water, particles of dirt, 
swarf, etc. Such things are difficult to spot if the chamois leather is dirty. 
The skins may be inspected in direct sunlight, which will help to show up 
certain types of particles by reflection.
